$comment: Render v2 registry: the ONE source for the view library. Edit here, then run python3 tools/gen_views.py (writes views/library.json, views/prompt/*.md, views/checkers.json and the SCHEMA.md views block). Plan: brain projects/calc/topics/openui-render-arch-plan-2026-10-18.md (START HERE v2, Appendix v1 §16); caps and locks: refine/REFINE.md F2 F3 F4 F5 F7 F11 F19, VISUAL-FIRST. Prop shapes = the P1.1 renderer's (views-lib.js reads them from library.json). props: ordered (positional order), JSON Schema each; {"x-any": true} = any shipped component. ships: P1.1 = drawn by views.js, emitted into library.json; planned = roadmap only (table in SCHEMA.md, never in a prompt).

layers.L0: primitives (escape hatch): build anything when no learning component fits
layers.L1: learning components: subject-blind, know data shapes only
layers.L2: renderers of engine data: every value comes from an engine result

semantic_figure_props.desc: figure marks only (Geometry marks, Graph nodes / edges): meaning, never style; they are not in banned_props and never apply outside a figure

wrong.desc: the picked distractor: wrong.error tag, wrong.text

key.desc: hidden answer values (key.v1); the gate drops any key ref, or literal equal to a key value, outside post

gate.desc: statement parses as OpenUI Lang (profile stem: no Mutation, no Action, no timers)
component exists in this library; args match its props, caps included (over a cap: drop, log too-long)
Query tool exists in the engine list; runs SERVER side; the browser gets results only
domain component: its checker re-runs the engine and compares
no key ref and no literal equal to a hidden value outside post; a Reveal body is a second program
recipe allows this stage; refs allowed in this stage
every state word in nodes / edges / marks / Legend items is one of marks
at most one Steps or Compare per root; one figure per Steps
no string holds a hex colour, px, an emoji, or an all-caps word over 3 letters that is no code

copy_gate.py on the view's student-facing strings: Flesch-Kincaid grade 2-4 on the whole view text (TeX and numbers stripped; skipped under 20 words), no term from views/allow/<course>-black.json (tools/jargon.py), no slot over its character budget, no blocking aiw.lint_view_strings finding

slot.desc: Slot convention (views plan Oct 20): any student-facing string may be the whole literal "$t.<id>"; views.js fills it from the view's t map (render option t: {id: text}), and an id with no text paints as an outlined empty box (data-slot=<id>) for measure_slots. Caps apply to the filled text, not the ref. components.<C>.words names every prop that carries student-facing text, with its UI role (shadcn naming) and expected word class; not_words lists the string props that carry data (marks, ids, TeX, coordinates), never words.

View.desc: The root: its children are painted in order, each into a slot reserved when the root arrives

Head.desc: Title and one-line subtitle of a view

Text.desc: A paragraph; **bold** is the only emphasis

Legend.desc: Legend chips, each "mark label"; the sample is drawn with the figure's own class

Table.desc: A small table: header cells, then rows of cells

Tug.desc: A push-pull rope: one row per factor, "label | move | up|down|same [size 1-9]"; the bar pulls right (up) or left (down); size is the bar's relative length; of = the thing pulled; net is the end knot (post only)

Flip.desc: Cards that flip from "you did" to "the fix": rows of [step, you did, the fix]; tap a card to flip it back

Math.desc: Display TeX; an identity it states is re-checked

Chips.desc: A row of small chips (givens, tags)

Callout.desc: A section with a rule and a short tag ("Where it breaks"), never a box

Steps.desc: A stepper: ONE anchor figure (Graph, Geometry or Doodle) drawn once for every step, the steps, an optional frontier row and status table; pips and Show all on top, Back/Next below. A Geometry fig keeps its structure: each Step lights its parts (lit; the rest turns pale), hides parts (hide) or relabels one (say), never a new figure per step. Draw objects from seg / rect / poly / arrow / label; label each quantity once ("R_1 = 2 Ω", "I = ?") so it gets its own colour, in the figure and in the formulas. No step numbers in any text. Example, 9 V across 2 Ω and 4 Ω in a row: s = Steps(g, [a, b, c]); g = Geometry("A 0,0; B 0,3; C 6,3; D 6,0; E 1,2.6; F 2.6,3.4; G 3.4,2.6; H 5,3.4; J 2,2.6; K 4,3.4", ["seg(A,B)", "seg(B,C)", "seg(C,D)", "seg(D,A)", "rect(E,F,$R_1$ = 2 Ω,fill)", "rect(G,H,$R_2$ = 4 Ω,fill)", "rect(J,K,$R$,fill)", "label(A,V = 9 V)", "label(D,I = ?)"]); a = Step("We add the two resistances: one row, one path.", null, null, null, null, null, null, "R = R_1 + R_2", "R_1 R_2", "Add the resistances", "R"); b = Step("We swap both boxes for one box with that total.", null, null, null, null, null, null, "R = 2 + 4", "R", "One box in their place", "R_1 R_2"); c = Step("Now you divide the push by the total.", null, null, null, null, null, null, "I = V / R", "V I", "Find the current", "R_1 R_2", ["I=I = V / R"])

Step.desc: One step: caption (one or two short sentences; with a Geometry fig the six Graph args are null: Step("...", null, null, null, null, null, null, "W = F s", "F s")), tex (one formula, TeX, no $), lit (a Geometry fig's parts this step lights, space separated: a point name "A", a segment "A-B", or a label as written "F" / "\theta" (or its symbol: "I" for "I = ?"); every symbol in tex is a lit label; empty = all lit), title (a bold heading of a few words, never a step number), hide (parts gone this step, same tokens as lit), say (labels shown with new text this step: ["I=I = 1.5 A"] = the label's symbol, =, the new text; a number in it is a given, never the answer), node marks "A:cur B:front", edge marks "A-B:tree", tags "A:0", edge labels ["A-B:new"], frontier, table rows

Hints.desc: A hint ladder: one hint at a time

Predict.desc: Pick an answer; the pick is posted with the answer ref to the server, the page never resolves or draws it

Reveal.desc: A visible locked row; its body arrives as a second program when the stage changes

Answer.desc: The boxed answer and one sentence

Doodle.desc: A small drawing when nothing else fits (visual first)

Compare.desc: Two side by side, stepped together

Assume.desc: "I read this as X" chip; a tap sends a refine request

Graph.desc: A graph: nodes "A 48 100, B 160 48", edges "A>B, A-C" (> directed), column labels "48 depth 0", marks "A:done u0:k1"; figure-only emphasis props layer "A:2 B-C:3" (1 = what the question asks, the default; 2 = given; 3 = implied or context). Never put layer 2 or 3 on tone=bad (red stays layer 1). and tone "A:c2 B-C:bad" (a figure palette hue: ink muted c1 c2 c3 ok bad mark)

Geometry.desc: A to-scale geometry figure: named points "A 0,0; B 3,0; C 3,4" (y up), marks seg(A,B) circle(O,2) right(B,A,C) dim(A,B,3 m) angle(A,B,C,$\theta$) arrow(A,C,$F$) label(C,top) poly(A,B,C) rect(A,B) (closed shapes: poly = the points in order, rect = an axis box from two corners; either may end with a label and then fill, e.g. rect(P,Q,$R_1$ = 2 Ω,fill); a resistor, block, cube or piston is drawn from these, never a named object); at most 16 points, 16 marks, 6 labels; a number in a label is a given, never the answer; a mark may end with layer=1|2|3 (1 = what the question asks, the default; 2 = given; 3 = implied or context). Never put layer 2 or 3 on tone=bad (red stays layer 1). and tone=<ink|muted|c1|c2|c3|ok|bad|mark|sky|amber|orange|violet|pink|cyan> (figure palette hues only; an arrow with no tone gets its own hue automatically, keyed by its label, so leave tone off unless a force must be a given color; ok / bad mean right / wrong, use them only for that), e.g. arrow(A,C,$F$,tone=c1,layer=2)

label_words.desc: the text argument of dim / angle / arrow / label: student-facing, may be a whole "$t.<id>" slot

FlowNet.desc: Flow network with flows and the min cut

FBD.desc: Free-body diagram; magnitudes from the engine

Timeline.desc: Ordered events on a line (history or motion)

rules: `rect(A,B[,label][,fill])` = an axis box from two opposite corners. Tilted? Use `poly`.
`poly(A,B,C,...[,label][,fill])` = a closed outline through 3+ points in order.
`fill` = a solid body or a liquid; no `fill` = a container, wall or cell outline.
`layer=1` = what is asked (default), `layer=2` = a given, `layer=3` = context (walls, ground, axes, supports).
One object = several primitives: a cart = `rect` + 2 `circle` + `arrow`; never a named mark (no `cart()`, `resistor()`).

Name parts so a Step can target them: a label (`cart`, or its symbol `m` for `$m$ = 2 kg`), a corner pair `E-F` (rect, seg), a centre `W1` (unlabelled circle). A whole object = all its tokens: `"cart W1 W2"`.
One quantity, one label: its colour carries into the same symbol in `tex`. Same `tone=` on every part of one quantity.

examples.idea: Combo: cart (lit / hide token "cart W1 W2")
Combo: a cell = 2 parallel seg of unequal length
Combo: tank = walls (layer=3) + liquid level (fill, layer=2) + dim
examples.src: g = Geometry("A 0,0; B 4,4; C 4,2.5; D 4.6,0; E 4.6,2.5", ["rect(A,B,layer=3)", "rect(A,C,water,fill,layer=2)", "dim(D,E,$h$,right)"])

examples.idea: Combo: pulley = circle + seg ropes + rect masses
One quantity, one tone: Riemann strips
examples.src: g = Geometry("O 0,0; X 4.5,0; Y 0,3.5; A 1,0; B 2,1.5; C 2,0; D 3,2.5; E 3,0; F 4,3.2", ["seg(O,X,layer=3)", "seg(O,Y,layer=3)", "rect(A,B,fill,tone=sky)", "rect(C,D,fill,tone=sky)", "rect(E,F,fill,tone=sky)", "dim(A,C,$\\Delta x$)"])

examples.idea: Symbol labels for a formula: trapezoid
examples.src: g = Geometry("A 0,0; B 6,0; C 4.5,3; D 1.5,3; E 1.5,0", ["poly(A,B,C,D,fill)", "seg(D,E,layer=3)", "right(E,B,D)", "dim(A,B,$b_1$)", "dim(D,C,$b_2$)", "dim(D,E,$h$,left)"])

misconception.desc: where the picked idea breaks, first; then the fix

predict-reveal.desc: ask a pick, the server marks it, the Reveal body arrives as a patch

steps.desc: worked steps, one at a time

twin-compare.desc: two methods or two algorithms side by side, in sync

slider-explore.desc: drag a parameter, watch the verdict change

answer-table.desc: the answer + the table that proves it (post only)
